correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the first-pivot rank gives independent left and right random-BST subproblems and the exact mean m_n(i)=mu_i+mu_{n-1-i}+n-1. The identity mu_{k+1}-mu_k=2(H_{k+1}-1) makes m_n(i) strictly increase away from the center. Explicit harmonic sums yield Cov(Q_n,P_n)=(n-2)(n-1)(n+1)/9, while uniform fourth moments yield Var(Q_n). The classical exact path-length variance then gives the stated correlation and limit. Exact enumeration through n=9 independently reproduces all finite formulas.

originality.rationale: The closest full sources cover random-BST path length and covariance among BST profile levels but do not retain squared root split imbalance as a joint statistic. The root recurrence itself is standard and the iid marginal path-length moments are prior art; originality is limited to the mixed dependence law, exact covariance/slope, monotone regression, and nonzero correlation limit.
residual_risks: Because the root decomposition is standard, older analysis-of-algorithms textbooks or exercises may contain this covariance as an unindexed calculation.
The Drmota--Hwang full text covers sophisticated BST covariance phenomena but not this root statistic; another older joint-search-tree paper could still encode the same moment in different notation.
The novelty claim excludes the classical mean/variance of path length and the standard first-pivot recurrence.

value.rationale: The first pivot is a single local choice, while total internal path length or Quicksort comparison count is accumulated over the entire recursive execution. An asymptotic correlation near 0.575 and linear explained-variance fraction near 0.330 show that this local split retains unexpectedly large predictive information. The exact slope and strict monotone-regression statement make the result reusable rather than a one-off numerical correlation.
